title: Implementation inventory — v1.0
description: Chainlink #55. The authoritative, machine-readable record of what this repository actually contains right now, replacing the stale '53 tests / M0-M1' prose summary #55 was opened to retire. This is a snapshot inventory, not a live report: docs/implementation-inventory.json is hand-curated (role + disposition are judgment calls a mechanical walk cannot make) and tests/test_inventory_drift.py fails the build the moment the repository's actual registered CLI surface or on-disk runtime-resource set disagrees with it -- so the inventory can go stale only by breaking CI, never silently. #56/#57/#58/#59 read this file and its sibling docs (docs/cli-contract.md, schemas/project-state.schema.json, schemas/consolidated-check.schema.json, docs/exit-code-contract.md) as their own required inputs; none of them re-derive this inventory from scratch.

inventory_version.description: Independent of product/schema/skill versions defined elsewhere (docs/cli-contract.md, schemas/project-state.schema.json, schemas/consolidated-check.schema.json) -- this document's own shape can change on its own schedule.

commit.description: Git commit this inventory was authored against. Informational provenance only -- the drift test compares against the CURRENT working tree, not this commit, so a stale value here is a documentation nit, not a silent-pass risk.

documentation_and_templates.description: docs/*.md entries: human-readable documentation and installed-template markdown that isn't a JSON Schema, so it doesn't belong in `schemas`.

test_count.description: Count of test FILES (tests/test_*.py), not pytest cases/subtests -- the drift test checks this against the filesystem; the completion report separately states the pytest case count from a live run, which this field does not claim to predict.

disposition.description: runtime-required: must ship in any working distribution. installed-template: copied into a target repo by `ligature init` (#58), not executed by the ligature binary itself. documentation: human-readable, informs but is not read by code. vendored-runtime: lives under vendor/ and IS read by runtime code. generated-projection: never hand-authored or shipped -- produced fresh from other artifacts, read-only output. test-only: exists solely to make the test suite exercise something; never installed or shipped. excluded: must never enter a release (caches, local state, secrets).

chainlink_milestone_id.description: The `chainlink milestone show <id>` this was read from -- the authoritative source, not plan.md prose (plan.md never defines M0-M4 as tracked identifiers; it only refers to them informally).

module.description: scripts/*.py path this gate's mechanized check actually lives in. Not frozen as public API (plan.md's own instruction: do not freeze module/gate implementation names).

cli_command.description: The flat pipeline.py subcommand that invokes this gate standalone, or null when the gate is checked inline inside a validate-* command rather than as its own subcommand.

name.description: The exact string argparse registers today, per scripts/pipeline.py:build_parser().

func.description: The cmd_* handler function name. Not frozen as public API.

stable_mapping.description: Cross-reference into docs/cli-contract.md's legacy-command mapping table -- the exact stable nested command, alias target, internal-operation note, or unsupported rationale. This is a pointer, not a duplicate of the contract; docs/cli-contract.md is the one place that mapping is spelled out in full.

note.description: Explicitly distinguishes a runtime-shaped example (e.g. a valid/ subdirectory showing a real artifact shape) from a deliberate-failure or stand-in fixture (plan.md §2's deliberate-failure regression convention, chainlink #12) -- both are test-only, but for different reasons, and this field says which.
